The Method

How the Challenge works

Not just Train → Track → Review → Progress — there's a whole curriculum behind it, one I've carefully designed myself!

1

Learn

Each week you unlock a new piece of the Glute Growth curriculum — a programme I've personally designed, built on the latest research in hypertrophy training.

You'll learn the real theory behind training intensity, progressive overload, technique, nutrition, recovery, supplementation and consistency!

The Challenge lasts 12 weeks — but the knowledge is yours for life. Think of it as an investment in your own education, not just your glutes.

2

Train

Follow your structured, glute-focused training programme at least 3 times a week.

3

Track

Log every working set, weight and rep. Progress needs data.

4

Review

Complete your weekly check-in so I can review how you're actually progressing.

5

Progress

Use the data and your personalised coaching feedback to keep moving forward — instead of repeating the same workouts for 12 weeks and hoping for the best.

The Arc

Your 12-Week Journey

Week 0

Fully set up, before you even start

Baseline photos and measurements, your programme built, your calorie and protein targets set — you start Week 1 completely ready, not figuring it out as you go.

Weeks 1–4

Build the foundation

Technique, consistency, understanding intensity, establishing nutrition, and learning how to track progress properly.

Weeks 5–8

Start pushing progression

Increase training quality, build strength, apply progressive overload, and identify where progress may be stalling.

Weeks 9–12

Maximise and consolidate

Push performance, refine execution, consolidate everything you've learned, and finish with the skills to keep progressing independently.

Not Just Results

This is bigger than 12 weeks of results — it's knowledge you keep for life

Each week you'll work through a focused piece of education designed to help you actually understand the process, not just follow it.

How hard "hard" actually needs to be Progressive overload Exercise execution Glute training principles Calories & protein Recovery Creatine / supplementation Consistency & adherence

By Week 12, the guesswork is gone completely — high-quality knowledge, real structure, and a clear, defined result, handed straight to you.

Questions

Frequently Asked Questions

Do I need gym experience? +

In-person: Some gym experience is useful, but you don't need perfect technique — I'll coach that.

Online: You should already feel comfortable training independently and have some familiarity with the main lifts / movement patterns.

Do I need to be an Anytime Fitness member? +

There's a reserved number of Challenge spaces available for non-members. Where applicable, gym access/membership can be included as part of the in-person package — ask me for details.

Can I do the online version from any gym? +

Usually, yes. Before starting, you'll need to provide a full equipment list / information about the gym you use, so the programme can be adapted where necessary.

What if I'm going on holiday? +

A short trip doesn't automatically rule you out. If you expect to be away for more than one week, mention this in your application so I can work out whether you'll realistically be able to follow the programme.

Do I have to track calories? +

Yes. Nutrition tracking is an important part of making sure you're getting enough energy and protein to support muscle growth. You'll receive personalised calorie and protein targets.

Is this a weight-loss programme? +

No. The primary goal is muscle growth. Building muscle may require maintaining or slightly increasing calorie intake, and some clients may see their bodyweight increase. A later fat-loss phase can be used to reveal more of the muscle built, if that's appropriate for you.

What if I have an injury? +

All current/recent injuries, pain or relevant medical concerns must be disclosed when applying. I'll assess whether the programme is appropriate — depending on the issue, medical or physiotherapy clearance may be required before participating.

When does it start? +

Monday 7 September 2026.

How much is it? +

In-person: £215 every 4 weeks. Online: £145 every 4 weeks. Both run for 12 weeks / 3 payment cycles.

What's the difference between the Challenge and normal PT? +

The Glute Growth Challenge is built around one specific outcome — glute growth — and follows a structured 12-week methodology and curriculum. My normal personal training service is broader, and can address multiple individual goals and changing coaching needs.
